On your computer, run “lifeos-bridge pair” and scan the code it shows.
The computer answered in %1$d ms. Bridge version %2$s.

The relay could not be reached. Check the phone\'s internet connection.
The relay refused this phone. It may have been unpaired on the computer; unpair here and pair again.
The message was sent, but the computer did not answer. Is it on, and is the bridge running?
The computer answered with an error (%1$d).
The key is deleted from this phone. To connect again you have to pair again. On the computer, also run “lifeos-bridge devices revoke”.
Once this phone is paired, the app asks for your fingerprint or screen lock when it is opened and after it was out of sight for this long.
Confirm with your fingerprint or screen lock to continue.
That was not enough to open the key. Please use your screen lock (PIN, pattern or password).
The pairing key on this phone can no longer be opened. Please pair again.
Pairing connects this phone to your computer. It is done once.
Scan the QR code it shows. The code is the key: show it to nobody else.
Compare the six-digit code on both screens and confirm on the computer.
The camera is used only to read the pairing code. Nothing is recorded or stored.
Without the camera the code cannot be read. Allow camera access for LifeOS in the phone\'s settings, then try again.
Point the camera at the QR code in the terminal.
Camera view for scanning the pairing code
This is not a LifeOS pairing code.
Check that your computer shows the same code. If it does, type “yes” there.
Waiting for the confirmation on the computer…
If the codes differ, do not confirm. Cancel and start again.
The computer knows this phone as “%1$s”.
The key can only be stored after you confirm with your fingerprint or screen lock.
This phone has no screen lock. Set a PIN, pattern or password in the phone\'s settings first; the pairing key is protected with it.
The relay could not be reached. Check the internet connection and start again with a new code.
The relay did not accept this code. It may be used already or expired. Start again with a new code.
Nobody confirmed on the computer within two minutes. Nothing was stored. Start again with a new code.
The pairing could not be stored on this phone. Nothing was kept.
LifeOS talks to the assistant on your own computer. Pair this phone with it once; until then you can still look around.
Pair this phone with your computer to see your own tasks, plans and courses here.
The computer could not be reached. Check the internet connection of this phone.

To show your screen time, LifeOS reads from Android\'s usage records how long each app was in front and how often the phone was unlocked. It sees nothing inside the apps. The numbers stay on this phone and, once a day, go to your own computer through the encrypted connection, nowhere else.
In the list, choose LifeOS, switch on usage access, then come back here.
This phone has no settings screen for usage access.

plurals.name: activity_chart_description
plurals.item: Bar chart of screen time over the last day. Tap it to see its apps below.
Bar chart of screen time per day over the last %d days, with the average as a dashed line. Tap a day to see its apps below.

resources.string: No app was used for a minute or more.
Send screen time and sleep once a day

Each finished day is sent once to your computer: the total, the unlocks and the 20 most used apps with their minutes, and each night with its times. It goes the next time the app is open and connected; the phone cannot send it in the background.
With usage access, nights you did not enter are estimated from when the phone lay unused.
No nights yet. Enter last night, or allow usage access for estimates.

plurals.name: sleep_chart_description
plurals.item: Bar chart of sleep over the last night. Tap it to see it above.
Bar chart of hours slept per night over the last %d nights: entered nights solid, estimated ones hatched, the average as a dashed line. Tap a night to see it above.

resources.string: If last night has not been entered, a silent notification at %1$s asks for it. It is planned on this phone; nothing is sent for it.
Asks for last night\'s sleep when it has not been entered.
How did you sleep? Tap to enter last night.
Which model each job of the computer uses, and its usage
Change a job\'s model here; it applies from the job\'s next run. "Back to the default" returns it to what the computer is set up with.
Saved. Used from the next run.

Your computer can reach this phone with notifications, also while the app is closed.
This build of the app has no push settings (or the phone has no Google Play services), so the computer cannot notify this phone.

A notification says only what kind of thing happened; what it is about is shown after you open and unlock the app. Each kind (chat, courses, coach, reminders) can be switched off in the system settings.

When the sign-in at the university site runs out, renew it here: the site\'s own page opens in a browser tab, you sign in there, and the new sign-in goes to your computer. Your password is typed only on the site\'s page.
Asking your computer for the sign-in page…
Sign in on the site\'s page. The browser brings you back here by itself (on some phones after a tap on its last page).
Passing the new sign-in to your computer…
Renewed. Your computer can fetch your courses again.
Your computer cannot be reached now. Try again when the dot is green.
The university site or your computer could not finish the sign-in. Try again later.
This sign-in attempt has run out. Start again.
The sign-in page answered for another attempt. Start again.
The university site did not accept the new sign-in. Start again.
No conversations yet. Start one with “New chat”.

Not sent: the computer cannot be reached right now. Your message is back in the box below; send it when the connection is back.
The computer did not answer. The message may still have arrived: if it did, the conversation is listed under Sessions. It is not sent again by itself.
This message is not in the conversation on the computer: it probably did not arrive. If its answer is missing above, send it again.

This folder cannot be used: it no longer exists, or it is not an allowed folder on the computer.

A newer LifeOS was built on your computer. It comes over the encrypted connection, is checked, and Android asks you to confirm the install.
Checked. Confirm the install on Android\'s screen.

Android lets an app install updates only after you allow it once: turn on \"Allow from this source\" for LifeOS, then come back and tap install. LifeOS installs nothing but its own updates from your computer.
This build cannot update itself: it is signed with a different key (a debug build). Install the release build once by cable; from then on updates come here.
The computer did not send the update. Try again when it is connected.
What arrived was not the announced file. Nothing was installed and the file was deleted.
The file is not signed with this app\'s key. Nothing was installed and the file was deleted.
Android did not install the update (cancelled or refused).

Nothing is sent in quiet hours, and coach notifications are at least two hours apart. Your computer keeps these limits.
